text:
ravi: Heads-up — noticed a spike in tail latency for us-west1 GPU pods around 03:20 UTC. Prometheus shows increased inference_service_queue_time and we’re missing runtime spans for ~30% of requests.
alice: Ugh. Any errors in the otel-collector logs or ingress? Can you paste a quick example trace id?
ravi: Trace id 8a3c...f9d2 from a failed request. The collector shows `exporter failed: context deadline exceeded` around the same time. Also saw some 502s from the gateway.
jonathan: Did we change sampling or the gateway config in the midnight deploy? I pushed a micro change to the otel gateway yesterday but it was just a healthcheck tweak.
ravi: Noted. I grepped the deploy: `git rev-parse HEAD` -> 4b2a8. The gateway config diff includes switching to the new grpc exporter endpoint and a lowered receiver timeout.
sre-bot: FYI: autoscaler triggered a scale-up at 03:18 UTC in us-west1 due to pod_cpu_pressure, added 6 GPU nodes. Some pods ended up on new nodes with older kernel -> networking flakiness noted in node-provision logs.
alice: That could explain packet drops to the OTLP endpoint. If SDKs can't deliver spans they may drop them depending on batcher settings.
marie: Can we check SDK batching settings in the runtime container? We recently changed the Python SDK batcher to `max_queue_size=2048` for throughput.
sam: Also confirm propagators. If traceparent isn't getting through our ingress (proxy trimming headers) spans will look disconnected.
jonathan: I looked at the ingress proxy config — it rewrites some headers for security. Might be stripping `traceparent` earlier this month when we added header whitelist. Opening a quick patch.
ravi: In flight workaround: lower throughput by forcing smaller batch sizes and enable realtime flush on error. Add env: `OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE=512`, `OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY=50ms`, `OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,baggage`.
alice: Can you post the minimal patch? I'll roll to canary in us-west1.
ravi: Patch snippet:
```
env:
  - name: OTEL_PROPAGATORS
    value: "tracecontext,baggage"
  - name: OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE
    value: "512"
  - name: OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY
    value: "50ms"
```
jonathan: If gateway timeouts are low, we might want to increase the collector export timeout instead of forcing SDKs to flush more often — otherwise we increase CPU and egress costs on GPUs.
marie: Cost concern noted. The finance ask last quarter pushed us to tighten SDK network retry budgets. But losing traces impacts SLO signal and alerting costs more in the long run.
sam: For alert tuning: current alert fires at p99 latency > 300ms for 5m. Given the autoscaler jitter and scale times, we should add a 3m no-change window before firing to reduce noise.
alice: Agreed. Also add an annotation to the Grafana dashboard to show autoscaler events and node provisioning so we can correlate.
jonathan: I'll update the Prometheus rule: `for: 8m` -> `for: 12m` for p99-latency-high but add a separate alert for span-drop-rate > 5% with `for: 2m` so we catch instrumentation regressions quickly.
ravi: After the canary roll I see spans returning and the exporter errors drop. Tail latency improved after the rollback to older kernel image on the new nodes.
marie: Can we add a synthetic trace test from the ingress -> runtime that validates header propagation and exporter reachability as part of the healthcheck? If it fails, degrade traffic before SLOs are impacted.
sam: Yep. We can run a tiny trace generator every minute and emit a metric `synthetic.trace.ok{region}` which Prometheus scrapes.
alice: Follow-ups: 1) patch gateway to keep `traceparent`, 2) short SDK config change in canary, 3) adjust alert `for` windows and add span-drop alert, 4) add synthetic propagation check.
jonathan: I'll open PRs for 1 and 3. Ravi can you do 2. Sam/Marie can you prototype the synthetic check? I'll tag you on the infra PRs.
ravi: On it. Rolling canary now. Ping me if the synthetic check triggers.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started by ravi for svc/inference-rt in us-west1 at 04:12 UTC :rocket:
alice: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone — good incident hygiene, pleased we caught kernel/provision mismatch before bigger SLA impact.
